title: Neuresthetics Genius Study person record (YAML front matter of people/<shard>/<id>.md)
description: Field meanings: docs/DATA_DICTIONARY.md. Coding rules: docs/CODING_GUIDE.md. Workflow: docs/RUNBOOK.md.

record_type.description: Fixed: tells the validator which schema applies.

schema_version.description: Version of the schema this file was written against. Bump in the schema and in every file together. 1.1 (2026-10-01): descriptions updated for decisions P1-P5 and S3-S4; no field or enum changes. 1.2 (2026-10-02): decision P8 adds basis recorded_interview (ceiling 0.7) and statement kind 'recorded interview'.

record_version.description: Integer, starts at 1. Add 1 every time the file's content changes in a commit.

review_status.description: Where the file is in review. Only a named human reviewer may set 'reviewed', with reviewed_by and reviewed_on (decision P5). Agents set only 'draft — unreviewed' or 'example — unreviewed' ('stub' for generated stubs). 'example — unreviewed' marks the worked examples.

collected_by.description: who ran the collection (person or agent)

collected_on.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) the first research run started.

last_updated.description: Date of the latest content change. Must match the newest change_log entry.

reviewed_by.description: Name of the human reviewer. Required when review_status is 'reviewed'.

reviewed_on.description: Date of the review. Required when review_status is 'reviewed'.

change_log.description: One entry per content change, oldest first: date, who, and a one-line summary.

record.description: Bookkeeping for this file: version, review state, who collected it, change history.

id.description: Person id from data/roster/person_ids.csv (lowercase ascii, family name first). Must equal the file name. Frozen once the file exists.

display_name.description: Name used in tables and prose. Usually the roster canonical_name.

rank.description: roster.csv rank (row order in the roster; not a quality ranking).

F.description: roster.csv F: how many of the five model lists named this person (1-5).

models.description: roster.csv models: which of the five lists named the person.

band.description: roster.csv band: frequency band derived from F.

status.description: roster.csv status: core / provisional / review / new — needs status / needs status (blank in v7).

field.description: roster.csv field (majority field across the model lists).

roster.description: copy of this person's roster.csv row; the validator checks every value matches

full_name.description: Full name as given in a reliable source, with titles removed.

native_name.description: Name in the person's own language and script, if different from display_name.

name.description: The alternative name, spelled as in the source.

kind.description: What kind of alternative name this is.

cites.description: Optional citation for the alias. Roster aliases need none.

aliases.description: Other names: roster aliases, birth names, Latinized forms, transliterations, titles.

identity.description: Who this record is about and how they appear in the roster.

date.description: Birth date. Record the calendar if the source gives an Old Style date.

place.description: Birth place as named at the time, with modern_name and polity_then where useful.

death.description: Death date and place. For a living person use UNKNOWN with how_known 'living as of <date>'.

first_lasting_contribution_year.description: Year of the earliest contribution listed in contribution.lasting_original_contributions. Drives era_bucket.

era_bucket.description: Bucket of first_lasting_contribution_year (decision P2). A year on an edge goes to the later bucket (1950 is '1950 on'). Birth year stays in basics.birth.date, so a birth-year version can be computed for a sensitivity check.

region_of_birth.description: Macro-region of the birth place, on modern borders, from data/reference/regions.csv (decision P3: UN M49 sub-regions; MENA = Northern Africa + Western Asia + Iran).

region_of_work.description: Macro-region where the major work was done. If split, pick where the main contribution was made and explain in note.

sex_as_recorded.description: Sex as recorded in the sources. Descriptive, for baseline matching only.

languages_of_work.description: Languages the person published or worked in.

occupations.description: Occupations held, in the words of the sources (e.g. bookbinder's apprentice, chemical assistant, professor).

basics.description: Dates, places, era and region: the descriptive frame for era- and region-matched baselines.

fields.description: Fields of work, in the sources' terms.

lasting_original_contributions.description: Each original contribution that is still used or built on, with year, kind, and what rests on it now.

evidence_of_impact.description: Evidence that the impact is lasting: named laws or units, textbook canon, assessments by later major figures, honours.

major_works.description: Main published works, lecture series, artworks or devices, with year.

honours.description: Honours, prizes, fellowships, offices; note any declined.

how_known.description: one or two sentences: what kind of evidence, and why this certainty

alternatives.description: competing values from other sources, each cited

value.description: The value, or a sentinel (TODO, UNKNOWN, BELOW_THRESHOLD).

definition_fit.description: Lane A: lasting original impact on documented criteria (not mastery without originality, transient fame, collectives).

contribution.description: What the person did that earns a place on the roster (Lane A definition: lasting original impact).

family_religion.description: Religion of the household the person grew up in (denomination, congregation).

family_religious_practice.description: How the family practised: attendance, observance, offices held.

parents_and_household.description: Parents, siblings and household members, with occupations.

household_circumstances.description: Economic and social situation of the household.

schooling.description: Each stage of formal or informal education, with stage, institution, years and ages.

early_mathematics.description: Highest level of mathematics met before about age 18, with ages and description.

early_geometric_style_reasoning.description: Any documented early exposure to definition-to-consequence reasoning (Euclid, formal logic, proof). Facts only; Lane B interpretation goes in lane_b.

early_science_exposure.description: Lectures, books, experiments or apprenticeships with scientific content before independent work.

key_early_reading.description: Books the sources say mattered in childhood or adolescence.

childhood_mentors.description: Adults outside the family who taught or encouraged the person.

languages_in_childhood.description: Languages spoken or learned in childhood.

notable_events.description: Other events in childhood the sources treat as formative.

childhood.description: Childhood and education up to the start of independent work. Lane A facts; Lane B's H1 test reads them.

unit.description: Fixed reminder of the unit of coding.

working_years.description: Years of the adult working life the coding refers to (e.g. 1820-1860).

nominal_affiliations.description: Memberships and affiliations (church, synagogue, society), with years and offices. Membership is not ideology.

self_described_science_religion_relation.description: How the person said science and religion relate, in their own words where possible.

primary_system.description: Dominant working metaphysics, as one of the 77 system codes. Needs basis; certainty may not exceed the basis ceiling, and is at most 0.7 if the record names a plausible alternative code (CODING_GUIDE §3).

secondary_system.description: Only if the person published in two systems. Otherwise leave TODO, or UNKNOWN with how_known 'no second system'.

candidate_codes_considered.description: Codes the coder weighed, with the reason for and against each. Fill this even when the code is still TODO.

A_locus.description: A Locus: transcendent person outside the world (0) ... immanent in or identical with the world (4).

B_cause.description: B Cause: miracle, petition, reserved exemption (0) ... law, regularity, no special cases (4).

C_ledger.description: C Ledger: reward and punishment of persons (0) ... impersonal consequence, or none (4).

D_authority.description: D Authority: revelation outranks observation (0) ... observation and reason outrank revelation (4).

E_scope.description: E Scope: hidden exceptions for an in-group (0) ... same rules for stars, insects, humans (4). Scored on the world's order: the same rules for every kind of being and event, and no hidden in-group exceptions in this-world events (fortune, protection, answered petition, miracles for the favoured). Salvation, reward and punishment, and moral-community scope are scored on C_ledger, not here (decision P7, 2026-10-02).

lio_axes.description: Position on the five LIO axes (0-4 scale, decision P1). Each score needs basis, certainty, cites and a rationale.

how_known.description: one or two sentences: what kind of evidence, and why this certainty

alternatives.description: competing values from other sources, each cited

value.description: The value, or a sentinel (TODO, UNKNOWN, BELOW_THRESHOLD).

mid_basin.description: v7.1 'mid-basin theist', by the test of decision P4 (2026-10-01): true when lio_axes A_locus <= 1 and B_cause >= 3, B scored on the person's account of nature (decision P6, 2026-10-02), both at certainty >= 0.7; false when A_locus >= 3, or A_locus <= 1 with B_cause <= 1; otherwise TODO (a needed axis is TODO, or both are scored at >= 0.7 but fall between the branches: A_locus = 2, or A_locus <= 1 with B_cause = 2), UNKNOWN (only if a needed axis is UNKNOWN) or BELOW_THRESHOLD (a needed axis is BELOW_THRESHOLD or scored only at 0.5). Deists usually pass (see METHOD). 'First-rank' is F >= 3, applied separately. TODO until the axes are scored.

statements.description: Verbatim quotations that bear on the worldview, each with citation, context, kind, axes touched, and how it was verified.

changes_over_life.description: Documented shifts in worldview, with year or age.

coder_notes.description: Free text: reasoning, doubts, what would change the coding.

worldview.description: The adult working worldview: the unit of coding. Not childhood religion, not heritage.

use.const: context only — never an outcome and never a worldview code
use.description: Fixed reminder: heritage is context only.

ethnic_or_communal_heritage.description: Ethnic or communal background as the sources describe it.

religious_heritage_by_birth.description: Religion of birth family (may differ from the household practice in childhood).

baptism_or_initiation.description: Baptism, circumcision, bar mitzvah or other rite, with date if known.

childhood_catechism.description: Religious instruction received as a child.

heritage.description: Ethnic, communal and religious heritage by birth. Context only: never an outcome and never a worldview code.

lane.description: Fixed reminder of which lane these fields belong to.

age_at_first_lasting_contribution.description: Age in the year of first_lasting_contribution_year.

first_evidence_of_lio_type_views.description: Earliest dated evidence of lawful-order views (law without exemption), with year and age.

sources.description: Every source cited in this file. Ids are S1, S2, ... and are local to the file. Every source must be cited somewhere, and every citation must point here.

sentinel.description: TODO = not researched yet. UNKNOWN = researched, no reliable source gives it (say what was checked in how_known). BELOW_THRESHOLD = some evidence, but under certainty 0.5, so the value is withheld (describe the evidence in note).

certainty.description: See docs/CODING_GUIDE.md. Worldview claims: 1.0 written profession, 0.7 consistent private letters, 0.5 scholarly reconstruction. Other facts: 1.0 established, 0.7 probable, 0.5 contested. Below 0.5: withhold the value (BELOW_THRESHOLD).

source.description: id of an entry in the sources list

locator.description: page, folio, section, letter number, paragraph, or URL anchor

value.description: The competing value.

note.description: Why it differs, or why it was not preferred.

alternative.description: A competing value from another source, with its citation.

claimRules.description: A filled value needs certainty, at least one citation and a how_known note. UNKNOWN / BELOW_THRESHOLD need how_known. TODO needs nothing.

basis.description: Evidence basis for a worldview claim. Sets the certainty ceiling: written_profession 1.0, consistent_private_letters 0.7, recorded_interview 0.7 (the person's own first-person words in a recorded or transcribed interview, decision P8), scholarly_reconstruction 0.5. Certainty may sit below the ceiling (e.g. at most 0.7 when the record names a plausible alternative score; CODING_GUIDE §3), never above it.

lioScore.description: 0-4 ordinal scale (decision P1, 2026-10-01): 0 interventionist pole, 1 leans interventionist, 2 mixed, 3 leans LIO, 4 LIO pole. Certainty is recorded separately.
